I will keep my 66 mu mainly in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the steadiest way for me to use my land and irrigation well. I will put 40 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same ground, then use the other 26 mu for cash and food crops: 14 mu of stevia and 12 mu of sweet potato. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it matters most for stable yield, and I will not push fertilizer blindly. For wheat, I will feed it enough nitrogen to hold yield, with moderate phosphorus and potassium, and I will irrigate a few key times because water is available. For maize, I will use hybrid seed and keep fertilizer balanced so the stand is strong after wheat. For stevia, I will manage water and potassium more carefully because leaf crop quality matters. For sweet potato, I will keep nitrogen lower than grain crops so the vines do not run too hard and the roots size well. I will mostly use rotary tillage for convenience and speed, but I will plough the sweet potato ground to loosen soil for tuber expansion. I will keep pesticide use practical rather than heavy, applying only enough to protect yield and quality.
